title: Cap. X Ultimum: if Fathers teach God foresaw the faith of those destined to life, they mean merits he himself would work by predestinating grace — Aug. De praedest. sanct. 10
pass_a_gloss: So also if at any time they teach that God foresaw the faith and obedience of those whom he destined unto life, and passed by those whom he foresaw would be unbelieving and disobedient, they judge that God foresaw no other good merits in anyone than those which he himself was going to work in the same by the grace of predestination. For by predestination God foresaw those things which he himself was going to do, as Augustine truly, De praedest. sanctor. cap. 10.
pass_b_english: So too when they teach that God foresaw the faith and obedience of those he destined to life, and passed by those he foresaw would be unbelieving and disobedient, they hold that God foresaw in anyone no good merits but those he himself would work in that person by predestinating grace. For by predestination God foresaw what he himself would do—as Augustine truly says (De praedestinatione sanctorum 10).
source_text: Sic etiam si quando doceant Deum praescire fidem et obedientiam eorum quos ad vitam destinavit, atque praeteriisse illos quos praevidit infideles et immorigeros futuros, non alia bona merita in quoquam praescisse Deum arbitrantur quam ea quae ipse in eodem per gratiam praedestinationis fuerat facturus. Praedestinatione quippe Deus ea praescivit quae fuerat ipse facturus, ut vere Augustinus, De praedest. sanctor. cap. 10.
